title: Network Hardware
intro: Catch up on the essential lesson knowledge with 15 auto-marked questions and a self-reviewed explanation.

questions.prompt: What is a NIC used for?
options: Connecting a device to a network
questions.answer: Connecting a device to a network
questions.feedback: The network interface sends and receives data.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the concepts, model and key definitions.

blocks.title: NIC
blocks.text: A Network Interface Card (NIC) lets a computer connect to a network and transmit/receive data. Interfaces have MAC addresses.

blocks.title: Switch
blocks.text: A switch connects devices in one LAN and forwards local data using MAC addresses.

blocks.title: Router
blocks.text: A router moves data between different networks, using destination IP addresses.

blocks.title: Wireless access point
blocks.text: A WAP connects wireless devices to a network, normally through the existing wired LAN.

blocks.title: Worked example · A student sends coursework to a printer on the same school LAN. Explain what the NIC and switch do. [4 marks]
blocks.text: The computer and printer are in the same LAN; the data must leave the computer. A NIC provides network connectivity [1] and sends the data [1]. The switch connects LAN devices [1] and forwards the traffic using MAC addresses [1]. Two distinct devices with two accurate marking points each.

items: NIC — Network Interface Card; connects a device to a network.
Switch — Connects LAN devices and forwards traffic using MAC addresses.
Router — Forwards data between networks using IP addresses.
WAP — Wireless Access Point; provides wireless connection to a network.
MAC address — Address identifying a network interface on a local network.
IP address — Network address used for routing between networks.
